verdict.rationale: Running a Windows environment in a virtual machine is a fair axis for an operating system, since an OS vendor can ship or support virtualization, so the story applies. The pack has no first-party documentation of Windows providing or supporting VM-hosted Windows environments. The only related item is a community anecdote about running Windows as a VM on a Linux host with unspecified tooling, which is a user-side arrangement and earns no credit. The WSL mention concerns Linux userland support, a different capability, and does not transfer.
